correctness.rationale: Exact elimination gives P(x)=x³−Lx²+Hx−HK and exact discriminant H(−4H²+QH−4L³K). Algebraic identity Q²−64L³K=(L−9K)³(L−K) yields necessary and sufficient cusp bounds, with nonpositive roots excluded. Both planar multipliers at a synchronous root are T′(r) and (2p−1)T′(r); the outer roots attract. At the rational witness, polynomial factors as (x−1)(x−2)(x−3). The exact derivative numerator/denominator and positive-coefficient certificate for 3−T′ establish global difference contraction and preclude any asymmetric fixed point. The accompanying standard-library verification program recomputes exact identities and finite samples; mathematical conclusions follow from the analytical proof, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: A motivated open modeling issue is whether density-dependent migration survival alone generates multiple stable positive carrying capacities when local patches have a unique global positive recruitment equilibrium. The theorem provides a sharp analytically classified bifurcation surface for a natural Hill-2 survival law, a genuinely coupled rational example with two hyperbolic positive sinks separated by a saddle and no asymmetric equilibria, and exponential synchronization. The structure exposes an ecological mechanism and parameter boundary not captured by an arbitrary finite simulation or routine stability check.
